_comment: Synthetic PagerDuty payload. Fictional tenant, service and versions. The scenario shape is deliberately adversarial: a version bump correlates with onset and is the obvious answer, but it is a red herring — the real cause is a lock-contention pattern whose cost grows with peer count. Included to exercise the verify phase, which exists to stop a plausible hypothesis becoming the root cause.

data.title: Routing peers stuck in a reconnect loop for one large tenant
data.description:
Tenant northwind-retail (approx 2,100 edge sites) has peers cycling Established -> Idle -> Established continuously since 01:40Z. Sessions come up, then drop before converging, then reconnect. No other tenant on the same fleet is affected.

Context offered by the on-call engineer who acknowledged the page:
- The route-exchange daemon was upgraded from 4.1.0 to 4.2.0 on this fleet nine days ago. 4.2.0 is the obvious suspect.
- However: this tenant ran 4.2.0 without incident for eight days. Their site count grew roughly 20 percent over the last week as a rollout completed.
- Restarting the daemon clears the loop for about 40 seconds, then it re-forms.
- A rollback to 4.1.0 was attempted on one node. The loop re-formed there too, though it took longer to appear.
- This tenant is the only one that does not have the route-suppression profile applied, so their edges receive per-site prefixes rather than a single default route. Product asked for that visibility explicitly at onboarding.
- The customer edge devices use a 30 second hold timer, which is not configurable from our side.
